The father's only daughter died of an illness and was buried there in the ordinary way. Coming into the forest, the father found that a brown bear had dug up her grave and was eating her corpse; he shot the bear and wept over her remains.

The illness had already caused many villagers to die and be buried in that same forest burial ground, so many other villagers have relatives buried there, exposed to the bears. Because bears will keep digging up and eating bodies buried in that ground—including long-buried remains, not just fresh ones—the father fears that other villagers will suffer exactly what he suffered: bears digging up and eating their buried relatives' bodies, desecrating the dead.
